chunks.text: JWT signatures protect token integrity. The server verifies an HS256 signature with its configured secret and rejects a modified token. Verification does not decrypt the token payload.
Access tokens expire after 30 minutes. The exp claim is checked on authenticated requests. An expired token produces HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer.
Registration stores only an Argon2id password hash. Login verifies the submitted password with the Argon2 verification API. Plaintext passwords are never stored.
Knowledge Bases belong to one user. MongoDB queries include both the resource ID and authenticated owner ID. Another user receives the same HTTP 404 as a missing resource.
MongoDB stores application metadata: users, Knowledge Bases, document records, page-aware text chunks, and completed question-answer history. It does not store embedding vectors in this system.
Qdrant stores 384-dimensional document chunk embeddings and retrieval payload text. Cosine similarity ranks chunks. Server-controlled owner and Knowledge Base filters isolate searches.

Ask history is a snapshot of completed questions and validated answers. History is ordered newest first and is not included in future question context. Deleting a source document preserves its historical answer.
Infrastructure as a Service supplies virtual machines, networks, and disks. Customers manage operating systems and application software; the provider manages physical infrastructure.
Platform as a Service supplies a managed application runtime. Developers deploy application code without maintaining the underlying operating system or runtime infrastructure.
Software as a Service supplies a ready-to-use application over the internet. Users consume the software while the provider manages application updates and infrastructure.
Original PDFs are stored on local server disk. Server-generated filenames prevent path traversal. MongoDB stores metadata, not PDF binary content. Upload size is limited to 10 MiB.
PDF extraction runs page by page. Each text chunk retains its document, source filename, chunk order, and one-based page numbers. Image-only PDFs without extractable text fail; OCR is not supported.
Deleting a document removes its local PDF, MongoDB chunks, and Qdrant vectors. A Knowledge Base containing documents cannot be deleted; delete its documents first.
The synthetic North service makes a metadata backup every 24 hours and retains each backup for seven days. Restore drills run on the first Monday of each month.
The synthetic North dashboard closes an idle browser session after 15 minutes. This interface inactivity timer is different from the JWT access-token expiration setting.
The synthetic South integration uses API keys that expire after 90 days. API keys identify automation clients and are distinct from user JWT access tokens.
The synthetic South service makes a metadata backup every six hours and retains backups for fourteen days. North and South have different backup schedules.
A CSRF token helps protect a browser form from cross-site request forgery. A CSRF token is not a JWT access token and does not verify a JWT signature.
A response cache temporarily reuses previously computed HTTP responses. Cache expiration is not the same as authentication token expiration or backup retention.
The synthetic public status endpoint permits 60 requests per minute per client. This rate limit applies to status checks, not to PDF uploads or question answering.
